primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy (CKD stage 5, end‑stage renal disease)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and potassium in 2 weeks, then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression; control blood pressure
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension (first‑line) and advises monitoring creatinine and K⁺ after 1–2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile and liver function at 3 months, then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 states all CKD patients should receive a statin for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 10 U subcutaneously nightly, titrate by 2 U every 3 days to fasting glucose 4.4–7.2 mmol/L
medications.duration: Indefinite — glucose monitoring and dose adjustment every 1–2 weeks, full review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control; metformin contraindicated at eGFR 12 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends tight glycaemic control in diabetic CKD; metformin is contraindicated (eGFR < 30) so insulin is appropriate

medications.dose: 800 mg orally with each main meal (titrate up to 2400 mg TID as needed)
medications.duration: Until serum phosphate <1.45 mmol/L, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Control hyperphosphataemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD‑MBD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises checking phosphate, calcium, PTH in stage 4‑5 CKD and treating hyperphosphataemia with binders

medications.dose: 0.25 µg orally once daily (adjust according to calcium/PTH)
medications.duration: Until calcium and PTH within target range, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat secondary hyperparathyroidism and maintain bone health
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends active vitamin D for CKD‑MBD when PTH is elevated

medications.dose: 0.45 µg/kg subcutaneously weekly (dose adjusted to maintain Hb 10–11 g/dL)
medications.duration: Until haemoglobin 10–11 g/dL achieved, then review every 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Treat anaemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ESA therapy after iron repletion when Hb < 10 g/dL in CKD stage 4‑5

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily (increase to 40 mg BID if needed for volume control)
medications.duration: As needed for edema/volume overload — review weight, electrolytes and BP monthly
medications.purpose: Manage fluid overload and assist blood pressure control
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises avoiding fluid overload in advanced CKD and using loop diuretics when needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR 12 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – high risk of lactic acidosis
Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention in stage 5 CKD
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain if needed

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
Guideline indication requires eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m²; patient eGFR 12 mL/min/1.73 m²

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure reading not available – assume target <140/90 mmHg and monitor after starting Ramipril.
Serum potassium, calcium, phosphate, PTH, ferritin, TSAT, and Hb values not provided – labs must be obtained before initiating ESA, phosphate binder, calcitriol, and to monitor ACE‑I safety.
Allergy history not documented – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or insulin allergies before prescribing.
Patient’s current use of over‑the‑counter or herbal products unknown – counsel to avoid NSAIDs and potassium‑containing supplements.
Prostate cancer status (early adenocarcinoma) does not contraindicate proposed drugs, but monitor for drug‑related effects on bone health.
treatment_summary: The plan follows NICE NG203 for CKD stage 5 with diabetic nephropathy. A low‑dose ACE‑I (Ramipril) and high‑intensity statin (Atorvastatin) are started for renal protection and CV risk reduction. Insulin glargine replaces metformin for glycaemic control. Furosemide is provided for volume management. Conditional treatments for CKD‑MBD (sevelamer carbonate, calcitriol) and anaemia (darbepoetin alfa) are prescribed pending relevant laboratory results. All contraindicated agents (metformin, NSAIDs, ACE‑I + ARB, SGLT2 inhibitors) are avoided. Monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, lipids, Hb, and bone‑mineral parameters is built into the schedule.
